scenes.heading: Galvanic cells
scenes.sub: How a redox reaction powers your phone
scenes.say: Every battery in your phone, car key or smoke alarm is a galvanic cell. It turns the chemical energy of a spontaneous redox reaction into electrical energy.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A water slide gets you down along a set path, not a wasted splash
scenes.science: A cell sends electrons through a wire instead of wasting energy as heat
scenes.breaks: on a slide one person goes all the way; in a cell, electrons leave the anode and different particles take them up at the cathode.
scenes.say: Dropping zinc into copper sulfate is like a cliff jump: electrons pass straight across and the energy is wasted as heat. A galvanic cell is like a water slide. Keeping the reactants in separate half-cells forces the electrons through a wire, where they can do useful work.

scenes.heading: Anode vs cathode
scenes.say: Remember: an ox, red cat. Oxidation happens at the anode, which is negative in a galvanic cell. Reduction happens at the cathode, which is positive. Electrons flow through the wire from anode to cathode, never through the solution.

scenes.heading: The salt bridge
points: Anions move to the anode side
Cations move to the cathode side
scenes.say: The salt bridge keeps each half-cell electrically neutral. Anions, like nitrate, drift to the anode side. Cations, like potassium, drift to the cathode side. Without it, charge builds up and the current stops.

scenes.heading: Building a cell from the data book
scenes.say: To build a cell, find both E nought values. The higher one is reduced at the cathode; the lower one is oxidised at the anode. Balance electrons, add the half-equations, then subtract: cathode minus anode.
scenes.caption: To build a cell, find both E° values. The higher one is reduced at the cathode; the lower one is oxidised at the anode. Balance electrons, add the half-equations, then subtract: cathode minus anode.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: A Zn/Zn²⁺ half-cell is joined to a Cu/Cu²⁺ half-cell. Find the anode, the cathode and E°cell.
lines: Cu²⁺ is higher: reduced, Cu is cathode (+)
Zn is lower: oxidised, Zn is anode (−)
scenes.say: Copper is plus zero point three four volts and zinc is minus zero point seven six. Copper ions are higher, so they're reduced at the cathode, and zinc is oxidised at the anode. Subtract: one point one zero volts.
scenes.caption: Copper is +0.34 V and zinc is −0.76 V. Cu²⁺ is higher, so it's reduced at the cathode, and zinc is oxidised at the anode. Subtract: 1.10 V.

scenes.heading: Watch for traps
points: No solid metal? Use Pt or graphite
scenes.say: Watch for traps. Never multiply E nought values; they measure pull, not amount. A negative answer means you swapped the electrodes. Use platinum or graphite when there's no solid metal. And predictions only hold at standard conditions.
scenes.caption: Watch for traps. Never multiply E° values; they measure pull, not amount. A negative answer means you swapped the electrodes. Use platinum or graphite when there's no solid metal. And predictions only hold at standard conditions.

points: Electrons flow anode → cathode in the wire
Higher E° is reduced; lower is oxidised
scenes.say: Quick recap. Oxidation at the negative anode, reduction at the positive cathode. Electrons flow through the wire, ions through the salt bridge. The higher half-equation is reduced, and E nought cell is cathode minus anode. Now try the practice questions!
